chunks: That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding the absent man, if he divorces his wife, then she counts her waiting period (iddah) from the day he divorced her.
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a wife if her husband is absent and divorces her?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of prominent Kufan narrators like Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the iddah of a ghayib (absent husband) commences immediately upon the pronouncement of talaq, resolving the juristic debate on whether the period waits for his return or death. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the immediacy of legal effects in divorce, distinguishing it from other schools that may require waiting for news of his whereabouts or death to finalize the iddah duration.
